name: How to Get Your ADU Project Started the Right Way

step.name: Step 1
step.text: So, you're ready to build an accessory dwelling unit! Taking that first step can feel overwhelming, but a smooth project always starts with a solid plan. Breaking the initial phase down into clear steps makes it manageable and helps you avoid major headaches down the road.

step.name: Step 2
step.text: First up is the feasibility check. Before you fall in love with a design, you need to confirm your property is eligible and what you're allowed to build. This involves a deep dive into your local jurisdiction's rules—whether that's LA City, Pasadena, or another municipality. This step clarifies crucial details like maximum size, height, and setback requirements. Working with a design-build firm from the start simplifies this, as they can handle the upfront research for you.

step.name: Step 3
step.text: Next comes the design and planning phase. This is where your vision starts to take shape. You'll decide between a detached unit, an attached addition, or a garage conversion. You can create a custom plan or, in some cases, use pre-approved standard plans which can sometimes shorten the review process. This is the stage where you align your goals with your budget and site constraints.

step.name: Step 4
step.text: Finally, it's time for permitting. Your completed plans are submitted to the local building department. State law now requires a decision within 60 days, but the process involves careful coordination. A professional who knows how to respond to comments from planning, building, and safety departments is invaluable here. Kickstart your project with confidence by having an expert team handle everything from initial designs to final permits. Call us today to learn about our integrated design-build process.
